title: Fast across a cell, slow across a body
hook: Diffusion crosses a cell in a blink. How long does 100 times farther take?

doesNotKnow: that diffusion time grows with the square of distance

misconception: Diffusion is like walking: ten times farther takes ten times longer.
objective: The learner can explain that the typical time to diffuse a distance grows with the distance squared, so 100 times farther takes 10,000 times longer, which is why diffusion works within cells but not across bodies.

claims.text: For diffusion in one direction, the typical (root-mean-square) spread x after time t satisfies x^2 = 2Dt, so time grows with distance squared; individual molecules arrive sooner or later than this.
claims.source: Berg, H. C. (1993), Random Walks in Biology, expanded ed., Princeton University Press, ch. 1; Nelson, P., Biological Physics (W. H. Freeman), ch. 4.

claims.text: D is roughly 5 x 10^-10 m^2/s for a small molecule such as a sugar in water.
claims.source: Berg (1993), ch. 1 (small molecules in water, D of order 10^-9 to 10^-10 m^2/s); glucose in water at 25 C is about 6.7 x 10^-10 m^2/s (Longsworth, L. G. (1953), J. Am. Chem. Soc. 75: 5705-5709). 5 x 10^-10 is a rounded illustrative value.

claims.text: With D = 5 x 10^-10 m^2/s, spreading 10 micrometres takes about 0.1 s and 1 millimetre (100 times farther) takes 10,000 times longer, 1,000 s, about 17 minutes.
claims.source: t = x^2 / 2D: (10^-5)^2 / 10^-9 = 0.1 s; (10^-3)^2 / 10^-9 = 1,000 s = 16.7 min (checked with node). With D = 6.7 x 10^-10 (glucose) the times are 0.075 s and 12.4 min.

claims.text: Spreading twice as far takes four times as long; on the plot the edge of the cloud is a curve (a parabola), not a straight line.
claims.source: From x^2 = 2Dt: t is proportional to x^2.

claims.text: Diffusion is quick across a cell but far too slow across a body, so large animals move oxygen and food by blood flow.
claims.source: Berg (1993), ch. 1; Schmidt-Nielsen, K., Animal Physiology: Adaptation and Environment (Cambridge University Press), chapter on circulation; Vogel, S., Life in Moving Fluids (Princeton University Press).

claims.text: The 30 molecule paths on the stage are seeded random walks (one dimension, 5-second steps) with the same D.
claims.source: Demo.tsx PATHS: Gaussian steps with variance 2D x 5 s; seed 424242.

recall.question: Diffusion spreads a molecule 1 mm in about 17 minutes. About how long for 1 cm, 10 times farther?
recall.why: Time grows with distance squared: 10 times farther takes 100 times longer, 1,700 minutes, about 28 hours.
